reviewPolicy: Curated historical archive. Each case includes a source URL and status label. Confirmed disclosures, official reports, secondary reporting, allegations, security advisories, historical precursors and defensive-history entries are distinguished. A source report does not prove an arbitrary learner or organisation is affected. Publication dates are shown only when separately known; event dates remain separate.
disclaimer: This is a broad curated archive of 119 documented cases and clearly labelled historical precursors, spanning 1836–2026; it is not an exhaustive list of every cyber incident ever. Some older records are historical reconstructions or contested accounts, and some 2026 records describe suspected exposures, vulnerability advisories or reported incidents whose scope remains under investigation. Incidents may be undisclosed, sources may be updated or removed, and claims vary in confidence. Each summary is paraphrased and links to a source. Illustrations are original generic artwork, not photographs from the actual incidents.

items.title: Creeper experimental worm — an early network self-replication precursor
items.summary: Creeper was an experimental program that moved between early ARPANET-connected computers. It is included as a cybersecurity-history precursor, not as a malicious cyberattack.
facts: IBM’s history of malware describes Creeper as an early self-replicating program that moved between ARPANET computers.
The program was a proof of concept and did not aim to damage or disrupt the systems it reached.
This record is explicitly a historical precursor and should not be counted as a confirmed criminal attack.
